packages.label: שִׁכְחָה וַאֲבֵדָה
packages.reason: שכחה (forgetting) and אבדה (the lost item / being in a state of loss) are declared explicitly equal by the Rebbe: 'הַשִּׁכְחָה הִיא בְּחִינַת אֲבֵדָה'. They are two aspects of the same spiritual reality — the condition of having lost one's pre-birth knowledge upon entering the world. שכחה is the mechanism (the act of forgetting); אבדה is the resulting state (being lost, having lost something). Neither produces the other — they are the same phenomenon viewed from different angles, making this a classic bechina. Polarity is neutral rather than evil: this is the natural human condition described in Niddah 30b, not an adversarial force. It is the problem the Torah addresses — the universal human amnesia about one's spiritual task — but it is not labeled as evil (sitra achra). The tzaddik's role (eitza, not bechina) is to reverse this state.

The 2-node component is retained as-is. Both nodes share identical essential nature: the spiritual amnesia that afflicts every person from birth. No merger is possible or needed.

The dominant node is designated as אבדה rather than שכחה because the entire teaching is structured around the concept of the אבדה — the lost item that must be recovered. שכחה is introduced as an explanation of what kind of thing the אבדה is; אבדה is the primary concept driving the teaching's practical directive (travel to the tzaddik to recover your loss).
